title: The Golden Ladder: Golden Cuts from Plato to the Eighth Dimension
description: The Golden Ladder, Version 2: the whole book. A ladder whose rungs are dimensions, with something golden on each. Opening: Map of the Ladder. Chapter 1, One Triangle, Three Numbers: the five Platonic solids come from three kaleidoscopes, and these from one triangle with a single number in its corner, 1, √2 or φ. Chapter 2, Silence Is Golden: the octahedron–cube sweep as weight shapes of SU(4), SO(7) and SO(9), with Fibonacci ladders of multiplets converging at the golden solids. Chapters 3 to 8 are DICTO's papers set as chapters: 3A The FUJI Family (#20) and 3B The Golden Split (#48), the 2D rung; 4 Every Platonic Solid Has Exactly Two Golden Cuts (#88); 5 The Red Queen 120-cell (#65); 6 All Five Golden Pairs Are Slices of Four-Dimensional Solids (#89); 7 Golden on the Octahedron, Silver on the Cube (#90); 8 Four-Dimensional Solids Whose Every Cell Is a Golden Cut (#91). Chapter 9, The Top Rung: E8 and its golden twist, the 240 roots folding into two 600-cells, one φ times the other. Version 2 adds the opening, Chapters 3 to 9 and the cover by DICTO. Version 3 re-lays the cover (more room for the top rung, the ladder centred) and the subtitle now reaches the eighth dimension, where the book ends. Version 4 cleans the photographs of DICTO's work in Figure 3A.1.
